title: Orchestration API + Client reconciler for safe model rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: We need a resilient, idempotent server API and SDK client reconciler that enables canary rollouts, A/B experiments, shadow traffic, and automated rollback while being safe for hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Scope: API endpoints for creating/updating/inspecting rollouts; client-side helpers (reconciler loop) that make operations idempotent and safe; permission model and audit events; automatic rollback triggers (error-rate, latency regressions, QA checks) and graceful promotion. Out of scope: UI console components (separate PM ticket), long-term analytics retention changes.
acceptance_criteria: Create/patch/get rollout endpoints implemented in runtime control plane and pass contract tests
SDK helpers (createRollout, reconcileRollout, promoteRollout, abortRollout) provided in node + python SDKs with idempotent semantics
Rollout objects stored with an etag/sequence and support optimistic updates; concurrent updates return 409 with helpful payload
Automatic rollback engine that can be configured by rollout policy triggers on metrics and passes chaos/regression test harness
RBAC scopes for rollout:create, rollout:update, rollout:view, rollout:promote implemented and enforced in Private/VPC mode
End-to-end tests for canary ramp (0% -> 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%) run reliably under CI with mocked metrics and simulate failure triggers.
design_decisions: Rollout object is first-class resource: {id, model_version, traffic_splits, policy, status, history, etag}
Idempotency: client provides a rollout_token for create operations; server stores token->resource mapping for 24h and returns existing if seen
Optimistic concurrency: all mutating endpoints require if-match header with current etag or return 409; SDK will automatically retry a bounded number of times with fresh read
Reconciler pattern: SDK exposes a background reconcile loop that compares desired vs observed state and issues small patch operations rather than replace operations
Auto-rollback decisions are policy-driven (thresholds + burn-in windows). The control plane exposes a /rollouts/{id}/evaluate endpoint used by both server engine and tests
Permissions: fine-grained scopes (rollout:create, rollout:update, rollout:promote, rollout:abort, rollout:view) to enable platform teams to grant limited rollout rights
Visibility: every change emits an audit event (actor, action, prev_state, new_state, reason) that surfaces in Console and private audit logs
api_endpoints: POST /v1/rollouts  -- create rollout; supports client_provided_token (idempotency) and dry_run flag
GET /v1/rollouts/{rollout_id}  -- fetch rollout manifest and status
PATCH /v1/rollouts/{rollout_id}  -- apply partial updates to traffic_splits or policy; requires if-match: etag
POST /v1/rollouts/{rollout_id}:abort  -- immediate rollback to previous stable variant
GET /v1/rollouts?model_version=...  -- list rollouts referencing a model version
POST /v1/rollouts/{rollout_id}:evaluate  -- run policy evaluation against provided metrics snapshot (used by tests and can be called by webhook)
GET /v1/rollouts/{rollout_id}/history  -- timeline of actions and audit events
sdk_helpers: createRollout(opts: {modelVersion, initialSplit, policy, token?}) -> {rolloutId, status}  // idempotent when token supplied
reconcileRollout(rolloutId, desiredSpec) -> status  // small-patch-based reconciler that respects etags and backoff
watchRollout(rolloutId, onUpdate) -> subscriptionHandle  // streaming status updates via SSE/ws where available
promoteRollout(rolloutId)  // permission-guarded helper that waits for finalization and returns final state
abortRollout(rolloutId, reason)  // records audit event and triggers immediate rollback
shadowTrafficClient.send(sample)  // helper that safely tags shadow calls so they don't count towards billing; includes opt-in header semantics
helpers will surface well-typed errors: RolloutConflictError, RolloutNotFound, PermissionDenied, IdempotencyDuplicate
idempotency_and_conflicts: Create operations accept client_provided_token; server responds 200 with existing resource if token previously used
Mutating operations are best-effort idempotent when using full resource spec, otherwise require etag: if-match semantics
SDK reconciler will perform exponential backoff on 409 and re-fetch resource before retrying; maximum 3 retries to avoid thundering herd
Race scenarios documented: concurrent promote vs patch - promote is last-writer-wins when authorized and increments sequence
Server-side garbage collection for tokens: tokens expire after 24h and are removed; docs will warn of eventual duplicates beyond TTL
permissions_and_audit: New scopes: rollout:create, rollout:update, rollout:view, rollout:promote, rollout:abort
Default mapping: org-admin -> all scopes; developer -> view/create/update (not promote/abort); operator roles -> promote/abort
Audit events emitted for: create, update, promote, abort, auto-rollback-trigger (includes metric snapshot and matched rule)
Private deployments: hooks added to KMS/HSM audit export to mirror audit events for compliance requirements
RBAC enforcement: control plane checks token scopes and returns 403 with actionable message listing missing scope
rollback_policy: Policy model: combination of hard thresholds (error_rate > 5% for 5m) and relative regressions (latency p95 increased > 30%)
Burn-in windows: initial canary window is configurable per rollout (default 10m) during which automatic rollbacks are aggressive
Graceful rollback: abortRollout triggers a staged fallback to previous stable variant with traffic ramp-down so in-flight requests are drained
Safety nets: if multiple rollouts for same model conflict, a higher-priority rollout (by sequence/priority) preempts lower-priority ones
Notifications: webhook and slack channel integrations for rollout lifecycle events and auto-rollback reasons
test_plan: Unit tests for API idempotency behavior and optimistic locking (409 scenarios)
Integration tests: reconcile loop against a staging control plane with simulated metrics producer to exercise auto-rollback triggers
Load test: simulate 500 concurrent create/update clients to ensure token deduplication and etag flow scales
Chaos test: randomly inject metric spikes and network partitions to validate graceful rollback and no double-promotes
E2E acceptance: example app uses SDK to perform a canary from 1% to 100% and validates audit events and metrics after each ramp
migration_plan: API versioning: introduce v1/rollouts endpoints behind feature flag for 4 weeks before deprecating alpha endpoints
SDK rollout: release node SDK v3.5 and python SDK v1.12 with helpers; keep legacy calls supported and map to reconciler behavior
Data migration: existing 'deployments' will be mapped to Rollout resources with created_at metadata and etags; one-time background migration job
Communication: announce breaking/behavioral changes to Dedicated/Private customers with upgrade playbook and manual opt-in window
Monitoring: add control-plane dashboards for token duplication rates, rollback triggers fired, and reconciler latency
